transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

My mom made me come in. She keeps standing in my doorway asking what's wrong, but I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. I can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I'm wearing the same clothes, I don't really change them. This shirt has a hole in the pocket from when I used to carry pennies around. Pennies are made of zinc mostly now, not copper. If you drop a penny in acid, the zinc dissolves and the copper shell just floats there. It's actually really dangerous for dogs if they eat them because of the zinc. My neighbor has a dog but it barks at the mail carrier every single day at exactly two o'clock. But um... yeah, I don't do my knitting anymore. Or my journaling. I used to go walking a lot, but I just sit now. I don't have the energy to do any of it.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?

No... I don't think I've ever felt like that. I don't have any energy. I usually just sleep. I have this heavy blanket on my bed, it's a weighted one, and it just presses me down into the mattress. Did you know mattresses actually get a lot heavier over time? It's because they absorb dead skin cells and dust mites. Dust mites look like little monsters if you put them under a microscope. We looked at pictures of them in biology in high school. Mr. Henderson taught that class, he had a lazy eye so you could never tell if he was looking at you or looking at the door. He used a lot of chalk on the board and the dust would just hang in the air in the sunlight... breathing in chalk dust can't be good for your lungs, it probably coats them like powder. But um... no. I don't get energetic or need less sleep. I just stay in bed.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or had thoughts or beliefs that others told you weren't true, like feeling people were watching or plotting against you?

I don't... I don't hear voices. But I know things that other people don't believe. Like my mom, she says I'm just reading into things, but she doesn't see it. Since I was taking those college classes, I've just... known. The school portal, the messages they send, and the clinic practicum people... they use these little wording changes in their emails and the comments on my assignments. It's to mark me. They're marking me as someone they don't want in healthcare. They change a word here or there, and it's a code. Codes are actually really fascinating, like the Enigma machine in World War II. Alan Turing helped crack it, and he was a genius, but they treated him so terribly afterward. It's awful how people treat you when they decide you're different or they don't want you around. Apples are like that too, you know? If one gets a bruise, it releases ethylene gas and makes all the other apples go bad faster. That's why they say one bad apple spoils the bunch. I used to eat a lot of apples, the green ones, Granny Smith. They're so sour they make your jaw ache right here in the back. But yeah... my mom says they're just regular messages. But I know what they're really doing. They don't want me there.
Did you start noticing these beliefs about being 'marked' by the school around the same time your energy and mood dropped, or did you notice them well before you started feeling this depressed?

I... I don't really know which came first. I just know it's all happening now. The emails started, and then I just... I couldn't get out of bed. Beds used to be made of straw, you know. People would just stuff sacks with hay or straw, and that's where the saying 'hit the hay' comes from. But straw gets really itchy and it attracts bugs. Ladybugs are actually really aggressive predators if you look at them closely, they eat aphids. Aphids destroy crops, especially roses. My grandmother grew roses, the big red ones, and she would spray them with soapy water to keep the bugs off. The soap breaks down their outer shell. Soap is made from lye and fat, which is so weird to think about, washing yourself with fat. But um... yeah, I'm not sure if the mood thing happened before or after the emails. I just don't have the energy to figure it out.
Have you ever had these beliefs about being 'marked' or targeted at a time when your mood and energy were normal, not depressed like now?

I don't... I don't really remember what normal feels like anymore. It's just all so heavy now. But before the heavy feeling, I don't know if the messages were there. Messages are so strange when you think about it. Like carrier pigeons, they used to fly hundreds of miles just to deliver a tiny piece of paper. Pigeons actually have this internal compass that uses the Earth's magnetic field. Magnetic fields are why we have the Northern Lights, the aurora borealis. I saw a documentary about them once, the sky was all green and purple. Purple used to be the color of royalty because the dye was so expensive to make, they had to crush thousands of tiny sea snails just to get a few drops. Imagine crushing snails for a dress. Snails leave that slime trail everywhere they go, it's like they're marking their path. But um... no, I don't think I can remember if I felt normal when I noticed the emails. It's all just a blur.
Has there ever been a stretch of at least a couple of weeks when your depression and low energy improved somewhat, but you still believed the school was marking or targeting you?

I don't think so... I can't really remember a time like that. A couple of weeks is a long time, really. It's fourteen days. Did you know that a fortnight is fourteen nights? That's where the word comes from. They used to measure time by the moon, the lunar phases. The moon controls the tides, pulling the oceans back and forth. It's so powerful, but it's just this rock floating in space. Space is completely silent, a vacuum. Sound needs a medium to travel through, like air or water. Whales can communicate across entire oceans because water carries sound so well. Blue whales are the largest animals to ever live, their hearts are the size of a car. Imagine having a heart that big... But no, I haven't had a time where the heavy feeling went away but the messages stayed. It's just all happening together, I think.

Before this current period, have you ever had a separate episode in the past—weeks or months ago—where you felt this same kind of deep depression and low energy, followed by a stretch where you felt back to your usual self?

I don't think so... I don't remember ever feeling this heavy before, like in the past. The past just feels like a completely different lifetime anyway. Lifetimes are weird to think about, like reincarnation. Some people believe you come back as an animal, like a cat. Cats sleep for like sixteen hours a day, which sounds really nice right now. They purr when they're happy, but also when they're stressed, it's a self-soothing mechanism. The vibrations are actually used in some kinds of physical therapy to heal bones. Bones are mostly calcium, which is why they always tell kids to drink milk. But a lot of people are lactose intolerant because humans aren't really meant to drink another animal's milk. Cows have four stomachs just to digest grass. Imagine having four stomachs, you'd always be digesting something... but um, wait, what were you asking? Oh, if I felt like this before and got better. No, I don't think I had a time like this in the past. It's just right now.

Roughly how many weeks or months has it been since you first started feeling this heavy and first noticed the emails 'marking' you—can you give me an estimate of the total time this has been going on?

It's been... well, this whole decline, the heavy feeling and the emails, it all started when I began the community-college program. That was about two years and two months ago. Community college is supposed to be this stepping stone, you know? Like a bridge to a four-year university. Bridges are actually incredible feats of engineering. The Golden Gate Bridge is painted that specific color, International Orange, so ships can see it through the fog. Fog is just a cloud that touches the ground. It happens when the air cools down and the water vapor condenses. Water vapor is invisible, but then suddenly it's everywhere, making it hard to see anything in front of you. It's dangerous to drive in the fog, people get into huge pile-ups because they don't slow down. You always have to leave enough space between cars, the two-second rule. But yeah, it's been about two years and two months since it all started.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or wishing you weren't alive during this time?

I don't think I've wanted to hurt myself... I mean, I don't really want to die, I just want everything to stop feeling so heavy. Heavy things are hard to carry, like backpacks. Back in high school, everyone had those rolling backpacks for a while because the textbooks were so thick. Textbooks cost so much money, it's a whole industry. They just change the edition every year so you can't buy them used, and they just shift a few chapters around. Paper comes from trees, which is sad because trees take decades to grow. The redwoods in California are thousands of years old. They have this really thick bark that protects them from forest fires. Fire is actually a natural part of the ecosystem, it clears out the dead brush so new things can grow. Some pinecones won't even open and release their seeds unless they're exposed to extreme heat. Heat rises, that's why the second floor of a house is always warmer in the summer... but um, no, I haven't really had thoughts of hurting myself. Just feeling really weighed down by it all.

{"intent": "Determine whether the depressive symptoms have been continuous throughout the 2+ years or have occurred as distinct episodes with intervening periods of normal mood, to assess whether mood disturbance has been present for the majority of the illness duration (relevant for schizoaffective vs. delusional disorder vs. depression with psychotic features).", "question": "Over these past two years, has the heavy, low-energy feeling been there almost every day the whole time, or has it

Every day? I don't really know... I haven't been keeping track on a calendar or anything. Calendars are kind of strange anyway when you think about it. Like, whoever decided February only gets twenty-eight days just made it up. And then leap years, because the Earth actually takes 365 and a quarter days to go around the sun. If we didn't add a day every four years, the seasons would completely shift eventually and we'd have snow in the middle of July. July is named after Julius Caesar, I think. A lot of the months are messed up like that, like October means eight, like an octopus has eight legs, but it's the tenth month. It's like daylight saving time, we just keep doing it even though it ruins everyone's sleep schedule. They always say it's for the farmers, but animals don't wear watches. Cows just need to be milked when they need to be milked. Milking by hand used to take forever, but they use machines now that just attach to them. Factories are so automated... wait, what were you saying about the two years? I'm not really sure if it was every single day, it all just kind of blurs together.

{"intent": "Determine whether the delusional belief about being 'marked' has persisted continuously and unchanged throughout the two-plus years regardless of fluctuations in mood/energy, which would support a primarily psychotic disorder (schizophrenia/delusional disorder) rather than psychosis occurring only within depressive episodes (MDD with psychotic features) or a mixture of both being roughly co-extensive (schizoaffective).", "question": "Thinking back over these two years, has your belief that the school is marking you stayed the

Well, no, not the whole two years. The stuff with the school portal and those practicum emails marking me... it's really been stuck like this, just completely fixed, for about the past two months. The portal is where they send the messages, you know? Portal is a funny word, it sounds like something from a sci-fi movie. Like a wormhole or a stargate that transports you to another dimension. Space travel is actually super complicated because of gravity. Astronauts float around, which looks fun, but it actually messes up their bone density. That's why they have to exercise constantly on the International Space Station. They have these special treadmills with bungee cords so they don't just float away while they run. Running is supposed to be really good for your heart, but it's terrible for your knees. My gym teacher in high school had to get both of his knees replaced. Surgery is so creepy, being put to sleep and not knowing what they're doing to you. Anesthesia is basically a controlled coma, which is terrifying if you think about it too much. But yeah, the emails marking me... it's been really fixed like that for two months.

Doctor: So for the past two months, that belief has been fixed. What about the rest of the two years—were there times when you didn't feel marked by the school, or was there some version of it the whole time?

Patient: I don't really think it was the whole time... I mean, I guess it wasn't. Time is so weird, you know? Like how an hour can feel like a minute or a year when you're waiting for something. Waiting rooms are the worst. They always have those old magazines that are like three years out of date. Who even reads magazines anymore? Everything is on our phones. Phones are basically tiny computers, but people used to have those huge desktop computers that took up the whole desk. My dad had one that made that dial-up sound when it connected to the internet. It sounded like a robot screaming. Robots are getting so advanced now, they have AI that can write essays and paint pictures. It's kind of scary, like what if they take over? There's this whole movie about that, but I can't remember the name. Movies are so long now, they're all like three hours. You have to plan your bathroom breaks so carefully or you miss the best part... but um, what did you ask me? I don't think it was the whole two years, no.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you believed the school was marking you, but you did NOT have the heavy, low-energy, depressed feeling at all during that same time?

Two weeks? Um, I don't... I don't really know. Two weeks is fourteen days, which is exactly how long it takes for a caterpillar to turn into a butterfly in a chrysalis. Or maybe it's longer for some of them. Moths are basically the same thing but they get a bad rap because they aren't as colorful. They just fly into porch lights over and over. Lightbulbs used to be incandescent, but now they're all LED because it saves energy. Energy is a big deal, like the power grid is actually super fragile. If there was a big solar flare, it could wipe out all the electricity on Earth and we'd be back in the Stone Age. The Stone Age had cavemen, and they didn't even have written language, they just painted on the walls. Paint is so messy, I tried painting my room once and I got it all over the carpet. The landlord was so mad, he kept my whole security deposit. Security deposits are basically a scam anyway, they always find a reason to keep your money. Money makes the world go round, right? That's what they say. But um... what were you asking? I'm not really sure about the two weeks and the low energy thing. I just don't know.

I really don't know. I haven't noticed anything like that. Noticing things takes so much focus, and my brain just kind of jumps around. Jumping is actually a really good workout, like jump rope. Boxers do that a lot to stay light on their feet. Feet are so weird if you actually look at them for too long. Like, why do we have pinky toes? They don't even do anything except get stubbed on furniture. I stubbed my toe on my dresser last week and it bruised so bad. Bruises turn all those crazy colors, like purple and green and yellow. Yellow is supposed to be a happy color, like the sun. But the sun can give you a sunburn, which peels and is super gross. Snakes peel their skin all at once, which is called molting. I saw a snake at the zoo once and it just stared at me without blinking. Zoos make me sad because the animals are trapped in those little habitats. Being trapped is just... I don't know, it's depressing. But what were you asking me? I just really don't know the answer to that.

I'm sorry, did you just ask me something else? My mind just went completely blank. Blank like a fresh piece of printer paper. We used to make paper airplanes out of those in middle school and throw them at the blackboard. Middle school was honestly the worst, everyone was so mean and the cafeteria food always smelled like old hot dogs. Hot dogs aren't even real meat, you know? They're just, like, random scraps all mashed together into a tube. It's really gross if you actually think about it too much. Thinking too much always gives me a headache anyway. But um... yeah, I'm not sure what you want me to say. I just don't know.

I'm sorry, what did you ask me? I think I missed it. My thoughts get so loud sometimes, it's like a radio playing in the other room but you can't quite make out the song. Radios are kind of obsolete now anyway, everyone just streams music on their phones. Phones are basically tiny computers that track everything we do. It's actually really scary when you think about how much data they collect. Data centers use massive amounts of water to stay cool, which is terrible for the environment. The environment is just falling apart, like the ice caps melting and the polar bears losing their homes. Polar bears have black skin under their white fur to absorb heat from the sun. Heat makes me so tired, I can barely function in the summer. Summer used to be fun when I was a kid because we had no school, but now it's just... I don't know. But what was your question again? I really don't know what you were asking.
Before these last two years, would people who knew you well have described your thinking or way of talking as jumping around like this and hard to follow, or is this new for you?

Um, before the last two years? I don't really know if they thought I was hard to follow. I mean, two years ago I was just finishing high school, and high school was mostly just people being really fake anyway. Fake people always wear way too much perfume, you know? Like that cheap vanilla body spray that gives you a massive migraine. Migraines make your vision go all blurry and you see those weird little zig-zag lines. Lines are literally everywhere if you look close enough, like the cracks in the sidewalk outside. You're not supposed to step on cracks or you'll break your mother's back. That's such a violent thing to teach kids, right? Why would a sidewalk hurt someone's mom? Moms are supposed to keep you safe. My mom bought me this shirt, but the tag on the back is super itchy. I hate tags, they just scratch you all day like a little bug crawling on your neck. Bugs are so gross, especially spiders with all those legs. But wait, what did you ask me about my talking? I don't think it's new... or maybe it is? I just really don't know what other people think about it.

{"intent": "Determine whether, during the same two-month period the delusional belief has been fixed and unchanged, the depressive symptoms (low mood/energy) have also been present essentially every day without break, or whether there were any days during that specific window when the heaviness lifted—this clarifies if mood and psychosis have been co-occurring for the whole duration (schizoaffective) versus psychosis persisting independent of m

Um, the last two months? If the heaviness lifted? I don't really know if it ever stopped. Two months is a long time to keep track of, it's like, almost all of autumn. Autumn is when the leaves change color because the chlorophyll breaks down. Chlorophyll sounds like chloroform, which is what they use in movies to knock people out with a rag. Movies always get that wrong though, it actually takes way longer to work in real life. Real life is so boring compared to movies, except going to the movie theater, but the popcorn there is always way too salty. Salt makes you retain water, which makes you bloated. I hate feeling bloated, it makes all my clothes fit weird. Clothes are so expensive now, even at the thrift store. People just donate literal garbage sometimes, like shirts with huge stains on them. Stains are impossible to get out if you wash them in hot water. But um, what were you saying about my mood? I really don't know if there were any good days or not. It all just kind of blends together.

Wait, did you just ask me something? I completely zoned out. The air conditioning in here is blowing right on me and it's making me shiver. Shivering is supposed to burn calories, which is weird to think about. It's like your body is a little engine trying to warm itself up. Engines always smell like gasoline, and gasoline actually smells really good when you're at the pump. Gas stations have the best snacks, especially those little powdered donuts in the crinkly bags. Powdered sugar gets everywhere though, it completely ruins black clothes. I mostly wear black because it matches everything and you don't have to think about putting an outfit together. Thinking too much just makes my head hurt, honestly. But um, I don't know what you wanted to know. I really don't have an answer for you, I totally forgot what we were even talking about.
In the past two months, has there been even a single day where you didn't feel that heavy, low-energy depression—even if just for part of the day?

Um, a single day without feeling heavy? I don't know, it's hard to remember days individually. They all just sort of stack up like plates in the sink. I hate doing dishes, the water always gets my sleeves wet. Wet sleeves are the worst feeling, it's so uncomfortable and cold. Cold weather makes my joints ache, especially my knees, which is weird because I'm only nineteen. Old people always complain about their knees, like my grandma. She used to knit these really scratchy blankets that smelled like mothballs. Mothballs are toxic if you eat them, but they look exactly like mints. Why would they make poison look like candy? That's just asking for trouble. Trouble is my middle name, well, not really, it's actually Marie. Marie Antoinette said let them eat cake, but cake is too dry unless it has a lot of frosting. Frosting is mostly just butter and sugar whipped together. But wait, what were you asking about days? I don't really know if there was a day I didn't feel heavy. I just can't remember.
